vuln_id: OSS-Fuzz issue 43534 / ARVO arvo:43534 / libbpf malformed .BTF.ext span validation

project.name: libbpf
project.fixed_commit_note: The staged ARVO patch adds earlier BTF sanity validation in `btf_new()` but does not modify the crashing `.BTF.ext` parser lines in `btf_ext_setup_info()`. This GT therefore grounds the bug on the saved vulnerable-source trace and ASan stack rather than treating the patch as a direct root-cause oracle.

classification.classification_note: The saved symptom is `SEGV` / `wild-addr-read`, but the project-side defect is an unchecked `.BTF.ext` header-derived pointer/span that lets libbpf read outside the intended section bounds.

bug_description.normalized: On the saved i386 AddressSanitizer run, the exact staged ELF witness survives `bpf_object__elf_collect()` with both `.BTF` and `.BTF.ext` present, so `bpf_object__init_btf()` calls `btf_ext__new()` on the attacker-controlled `.BTF.ext` section. In the vulnerable source, `btf_ext__new()` copies those raw bytes and `btf_ext_parse_hdr()` performs only shallow header checks (magic, version, flags, and that `data_size >= hdr_len`). `btf_ext_setup_func_info()` then copies attacker-controlled `func_info_off` and `func_info_len` from the same header, and `btf_ext_setup_info()` computes `info = btf_ext->data + btf_ext->hdr->hdr_len + ext_sec->off` plus `info_left = ext_sec->len`. The only bounds guard compares `btf_ext->data + btf_ext->data_size` against `info + ext_sec->len` after that pointer arithmetic instead of validating the offset/length tuple in overflow-safe integer form. On the reproduced 32-bit build, the malformed header values leave an invalid `sinfo` pointer un-rejected, and the first dereference `num_records = sinfo->num_info` faults exactly at `src/btf.c:2656`, matching the saved ASan stack `btf_ext_setup_info -> btf_ext_setup_func_info -> btf_ext__new -> bpf_object__init_btf`.

source.description: First project-side consumption of the attacker-controlled `.BTF.ext` section on the crashing path. After ELF section collection and successful `.BTF` loading, `bpf_object__init_btf()` forwards the raw `.BTF.ext` bytes and size into libbpf's BTF.ext parser.
source.value_from: The harness in `bpf-object-fuzzer.c:33` passes the exact staged `poc` buffer and size to `bpf_object__open_mem(data, size, &opts)`. `bpf_object__elf_collect()` later records the witness's `.BTF.ext` section as `btf_ext_data`, and line 2748 is the first project statement that consumes that section on the crashing path.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.code:
info = btf_ext->data + btf_ext->hdr->hdr_len + ext_sec->off;
info_left = ext_sec->len;
tainted_value_origin.description: This expression combines the attacker-controlled `.BTF.ext` header fields `hdr_len`, `func_info_off`, and `func_info_len` into the candidate `func_info` start pointer and remaining span that later drive the faulty bounds check and sink dereference.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: These values come from the same raw `.BTF.ext` bytes copied in `btf_ext__new()`. `btf_ext_parse_hdr()` only checks the outer header envelope before `btf_ext_setup_func_info()` and `btf_ext_setup_info()` use the internal subsection fields.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The only span guard compares raw pointers after attacker-controlled pointer arithmetic instead of validating the `.BTF.ext` offset/length tuple in overflow-safe integer form. A malformed header can therefore leave `info` or `info + ext_sec->len` outside the real allocation without being rejected here.
root_cause.note: The reproduced job is `libfuzzer_asan_i386_libbpf`, so this arithmetic runs in a 32-bit address space. On the saved crash path the predicate is false, execution continues, and later code trusts `sinfo` anyway.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The unchecked `sinfo` pointer is dereferenced as the first `struct btf_ext_info_sec` header, and reading `num_info` triggers the saved wild-address read.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address ... READ` at `/src/libbpf/src/btf.c:2656:24` with stack `btf_ext_setup_info -> btf_ext_setup_func_info -> btf_ext__new -> bpf_object__init_btf`.

parser_admitted.description: This dispatch is reached only after ELF section scanning has accepted the witness far enough to keep both `.BTF` and `.BTF.ext` as `Elf_Data *` records. On the saved run, that admission step is what hands the attacker-controlled BTF sections to `bpf_object__init_btf()`.

evidence_limitations: Read-only generic ELF tools (`file`, `readelf`, `objdump`) report the staged witness has corrupted section-header metadata, including an invalid `e_shentsize`, so Stage 02 grounds the tainted `.BTF.ext` values at the source statements that consume `btf_ext_data->d_buf` rather than claiming a full standalone section-table decode.
The staged ARVO patch metadata is broader and earlier than the witnessed crash path. This GT therefore uses the vulnerable-source trace and saved ASan stack as the authoritative causal evidence.

fine_trace.note: Source. After ELF section collection and successful `.BTF` loading earlier in the same function, this call forwards the attacker-controlled `.BTF.ext` section bytes and size into libbpf's dedicated BTF.ext parser.
Copies the raw `.BTF.ext` bytes into parser-owned storage. Because `struct btf_ext` aliases `data` and `hdr` through a union, later header-field reads interpret these same copied attacker bytes.

Materializes the attacker-controlled `func_info` subsection offset and length from the copied header. The earlier `btf_ext_parse_hdr()` call validated only magic/version/flags and minimum header coverage, so these internal bounds survive unchecked into `ext_sec`.

fine_trace.code:
info = btf_ext->data + btf_ext->hdr->hdr_len + ext_sec->off;
info_left = ext_sec->len;
fine_trace.note: Computes the candidate `func_info` start pointer and claimed span directly from attacker-controlled header values: the basis is `btf_ext->data`, while the displacement is `hdr_len + func_info_off` and the remaining span is `func_info_len`.

Root cause. This is the only bounds check on the derived span, but it performs the comparison only after the attacker-controlled pointer arithmetic has already happened. On the reproduced i386 path, the malformed header values leave this predicate false, so the invalid `func_info` span is accepted instead of rejected.
Because step 5 did not reject the candidate span, the parser advances past the record-size word and reinterprets `info + 4` as the first `struct btf_ext_info_sec *sinfo`.

Sink. The first read from the unchecked `sinfo` pointer faults here. The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `SEGV on unknown address ... READ` at this exact line with stack `btf_ext_setup_info -> btf_ext_setup_func_info -> btf_ext__new -> bpf_object__init_btf`.

poc.trigger: The exact staged malformed ELF witness is passed to `bpf_object__open_mem()`, survives libelf admission and section collection far enough that `bpf_object__init_btf()` invokes `btf_ext__new()` on its `.BTF.ext` bytes, and on the saved i386 ASan run those header-derived values drive `btf_ext_setup_info()` into the invalid `sinfo->num_info` read at `src/btf.c:2656`.

format.name: ELF64 little-endian relocatable eBPF object with malformed .BTF.ext metadata
format.contract: Exactly the staged `poc` file. Stage 01 proves only this witness and this parser state: libbpf reaches `.BTF.ext` parsing, accepts the header-derived `func_info` span far enough to assign `sinfo = info + 4`, and then crashes on `num_records = sinfo->num_info`. Because generic standalone ELF tools report corrupted section-header metadata on the file, this contract does not generalize beyond the saved witness.
